text:
Maria: FYI — LumenX onboarding hitting repeated 401s immediately after the SDK init in staging. They say first request succeeds then next few fail. Repro steps + logs below.

Tom: Can you paste the exact SDK config they used and a raw auth header from a failing request?

Maria: repro (from their env):
```bash
# SDK bootstrap
node app.js --env=staging
# request that sometimes 200 then 401
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral-token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They rotated keys and still see the window. No proxies on their side besides Cloudflare.

Ashley: Quick checklist — usually this is either:
- ephemeral token TTL too short or clock skew
- edge dropping Authorization on follow-up preflight/redirects
- client reusing a cached handshake session with old token

Maria: attaching a trimmed network trace they sent (redacted):
```
> POST /v1/generate 200 OK
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...abc exp=169...
<response ok>

> POST /v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...abc exp=169...
<response {"error":"unauthorized"}>
```
They insist token looks identical between calls.

Tom: Could be our token-introspection TTL mismatch between auth service and gateway. @infra-bot can you confirm if staging auth cache TTL was changed last 48h?

infra-bot: staging-auth-cache TTL = 30s (default). No recent changes in the last 7 days. Deployment 2026-03-20 rolled service/auth 1.12.3.

Ashley: Two other quick probes:
1) ask them to enable SDK debug flag (prints token generation + clock)
2) have them run a simple loop with 1s interval to check deterministic window:
```js
const sdk = new RedwoodSDK({debug: true});
setInterval(async () => { try { await sdk.generate('ping'); console.log('ok'); } catch (e) { console.log('fail', e.message); } }, 1000);
```

Maria: I asked them to run that and they posted results: ok, ok, fail, fail, ok, ok — pattern looks periodic.

Sam: That periodic pattern screams cached-introspection TTL or a token revocation window at the gateway. Also check for loadbalancer sticky session failover — if token bound to a node with ephemeral state.

Tom: Good point. @ops-bot roll call: were there any LB reshuffles causing client to hit different gateway instances around 10–15s windows?

ops-bot: No LB updates in the past 24h. There was a surge at 2026-03-21T14:12Z causing autoscale, but no config changes.

Ashley: Another hypothesis — client SDK may be reusing an in-memory cached handshake that expects a per-node KV to validate token. If the node handling the first request changes, next node might not have the handshake established. We had a similar issue with edge-sdk v0.9.2.

Maria: They are on lite-web SDK v0.9.2 — oh.

Tom: If that's the case, short-term workaround: set SDK to prefer single connection (disable connection reuse) or increase token TTL on staging to 120s while we triage. Long-term: make token validation stateless or warm peer KV on new nodes.

Maria: I asked LumenX to try: 1) upgrade to v0.9.3 (we patched handshake reuse), or 2) set env REDWOOD_TOKEN_TTL=120. They replied they'll try upgrade first.

Sam: Action items:
- Maria: coordinate with LumenX to run upgrade + sdk debug (ETA 2h)
- Tom: follow up on auth-introspection logs and see if we have mismatched cache hits (ETA 4h)
- Ashley: prepare quick rollback/playbook note for support if they see regressions (ETA 1h)

Maria: noted. I'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

Tom: If upgrade doesn't fix it, we'll enable a temporary bypass on staging to force stateless validation for that tenant — notify @Sam before.

Maria: LumenX ran the upgrade and the loop now reports: ok, ok, ok, ok — looks resolved. They will remain in staging for 24h and then signal for prod onboarding.

Sam: Great. Please capture any SDK debug dumps they saved and add to their account ticket for postmortem.

Maria: done — uploaded logs to ticket #CS-9812 and left notes about handshake fix in the onboarding doc. Closing this thread once they go prod.

Tom: Thanks all.
